newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman cenbank governor says keeps eye on IPO loans.
newsitem.headline: Oman cenbank governor says keeps eye on IPO loans.

text.p: The Central Bank of Oman (CBO) is keeping a close eye on commercial banks to prevent them from granting big loans to customers specifically to fund initial public offering purchases, its executive president said.

"Some commercial banks in Oman have recently increased their lending activities to customers to apply for new shares which they do not receive. But the customers still have to pay interest to the banks," said Hamoud bin Sanjour Hashem on Monday.
"This trend is being closely monitored by the CBO," he said.
Hashem said the increased lending for IPOs would lead to vast oversubscription of shares and could artificially raise the price of shares once they were floated.

All of the more than 12 initial public offerings (IPOs) in Oman so far this year have been heavily oversubscribed as investors hope for quick, large returns. Some issues have been oversubscribed by almost 100 times.

Analysts said many investors had taken bank loans to finance the share purchases, but as many were allotted only a portion of applications, there was concern they would be unable to pay the interest on the loans.
Hashem said these investors would still have to pay interest on the loans they could have invested in profitable fields. He said the loans would also reduce investment in other sectors.
The Central Bank has told commercial banks that customers must deposit a sum with them equal to at least 50 percent of the intended subscription in an IPO, the executive president added.
